title: Higenamine alleviates abdominal aortic aneurysm by regulating oxidative stress and inflammation against VSMC apoptosis.
authors: Li, Jing-Yu; Li, Jing; Guo, Rui-Kang; Qi, Zhen
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然生物碱Higenamine对腹主动脉瘤的治疗作用，聚焦VSMC凋亡与炎症信号通路，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive vascular disease marked by apoptosis and phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), degradation of the extracellular matrix (ECM), and chronic inflammation. Currently, no pharmacological treatments are available. This work investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of the natural alkaloid higenamine (HG) in AAA. METHODS: H(2)O(2)- and LPS-induced VSMCs models were used to assess HG's effects on apoptosis, phenotype, and inflammation. An elastase-induced AAA mouse model evaluated its efficacy in vivo. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, dynamics simulations and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were conducted to elucidate targets and pathways. Mechanistic studies employed Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunohistochemistry to evaluate the AKT/mTOR and NF-kappaB/PTGS2 signaling axes. RESULTS: HG improved VSMCs viability under oxidative stress, reduced ROS and apoptosis, and preserved contractile markers (CNN1, SM22alpha). In vivo, HG reduced aortic dilation, elastin degradation, and the expression of MMP2 and cleaved caspase-3. Network analysis identified 25 HG-AAA overlapping targets enriched in PI3K-AKT/mTOR pathways, highlighting AKT1 and PTGS2. Molecular docking and CETSA confirmed that HG binds strongly to these proteins. HG enhanced AKT/mTOR phosphorylation in VSMCs in a PI3K-dependent manner. In the LPS model, HG suppressed TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, p-NF-kappaB, and PTGS2 expression, and reduced NF-kappaB nuclear translocation. IHC and Western blot confirmed that HG restored AKT/mTOR activation and reduced PTGS2 in AAA tissues in a dose-dependent manner. CONCLUSIONS: HG attenuates AAA progression by activating the AKT/mTOR pathway and inhibiting the NF-kappaB/PTGS2 axis, offering vascular protection through anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. These findings support HG as a promising multi-target natural compound for AAA therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景：腹主动脉瘤（AAA）是一种进行性血管疾病，其特征为血管平滑肌细胞（VSMCs）的凋亡和表型转化、细胞外基质（ECM）降解以及慢性炎症。目前尚无药物治疗可用。本研究探讨了天然生物碱 higenamine（HG）在AAA中的治疗潜力及分子机制。方法：采用H(2)O(2)和LPS诱导的VSMCs模型评估HG对凋亡、表型和炎症的影响；利用弹性蛋白酶诱导的AAA小鼠模型评估其体内疗效。通过网络药理学、分子对接、动力学模拟和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）阐明靶点和通路。机制研究采用Western blot、RT-qPCR和免疫组化评估AKT/mTOR和NF-kappaB/PTGS2信号轴。结果：HG在氧化应激下改善VSMCs活力，减少ROS和凋亡，并保留收缩标志物（CNN1、SM22alpha）。体内实验中，HG减少主动脉扩张、弹性蛋白降解以及MMP2和cleaved caspase-3的表达。网络分析识别出25个HG-AAA重叠靶点，富集于PI3K-AKT/mTOR通路，突出AKT1和PTGS2。分子对接和CETSA证实HG与这些蛋白强结合。HG以PI3K依赖性方式增强VSMCs中AKT/mTOR磷酸化。在LPS模型中，HG抑制TNF-alpha、IL-1beta、IL-6、p-NF-kappaB和PTGS2表达，并减少NF-kappaB核转位。免疫组化和Western blot证实HG以剂量依赖性方式恢复AAA组织中AKT/mTOR激活并降低PTGS2。结论：HG通过激活AKT/mTOR通路和抑制NF-kappaB/PTGS2轴来减轻AAA进展，通过抗凋亡和抗炎机制提供血管保护。这些发现支持HG作为AAA治疗中一种有前景的多靶点天然化合物。
